subject: Apexx11b elevated timeouts — recovery actions and closure
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <pri.shah@atlasdata.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Observed elevated timeouts for Apexx11b — immediate mitigations

Hi Priya,

We observed an increase in 5xx/timeouts affecting requests served by Apexx11b for Atlas Data between 07:45–08:10 PDT this morning. You may have seen partial failures in batch inference and some streaming responses timing out.

What we did immediately:
- Identified a change in tail-latency correlated with a new kernel selection path triggered for long-context requests.
- Rolled back the kernel selection change to the prior (stable) path at 08:02 PDT which reduced new error rates.
- Scoped affected customers and traffic; Atlas Data saw ~3.2% elevated errors during the window.

Next steps (initial):
1) We've attached a short log excerpt showing 5xx timestamps and the rollback marker. (attachment: apexx_error_wave_log_excerpt.txt)
2) Our infra team is keeping a real-time watch and will run a focused verification across your routes for the next 24 hours.
3) We'll follow up with a short postmortem including root cause and a remediation plan by EOD tomorrow.

I understand this disruption impacts your pipelines; we are prioritizing this with on-call engineering and will coordinate any compensation/credits with your account team.

Short ask: please confirm whether you observed any customer-facing impact beyond what we reported (drop in throughput, spikes in user errors, or data integrity concerns).

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll get you a clear timeline and closure.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Shah <pri.shah@atlasdata.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Jeff Nguyen <jeff.nguyen@atlasdata.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observed elevated timeouts for Apexx11b — immediate mitigations

Thanks Mina — appreciate the fast response.

Impact here: several ad-hoc analytics jobs retried and one customer pipeline reported a failed webhook that caused a downstream job to abort (we have logs, I can share if useful). Throughput dipped ~8% for the time window you noted.

Questions:
- Can you share the exact rollback timestamp and whether any cached KV state was invalidated?
- If credits are on the table, what’s the process/timeline to apply them?

We’ll collect logs for the failed webhook and send them to the address you provide.

— Priya
Director, Platform Engineering
Atlas Data

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observed elevated timeouts for Apexx11b — immediate mitigations

Re-posting internal notes / action items from the incident bridge this morning. (Keeping Priya and Atlas updated via Mina.)

Timeline summary:
- 07:42 PDT: Monitoring alerted to increase in Apexx11b tail latencies and 5xx counts for long-context endpoints.
- 07:50 PDT: On-call perf engineer began triage; identified kernel-selection code path that was selected for requests > 4k tokens.
- 08:02 PDT: Rollback of kernel selector to prior stable commit; traffic routed back to stable path by 08:06 PDT.
- 08:10 PDT: Error rates returned to baseline ~90th pct latency pre-incident.

Root cause (preliminary):
- A performance path intended to optimize attention computation under long sequences regressed under specific memory allocation patterns, causing intermittent OOM-like retries that surfaced as 5xx/timeouts.

Planned remediation (next 72 hours):
- Karthik to run a controlled ablation test of the kernel-selection heuristic on a canary fleet and reproduce the allocation pattern. (owner: karthik.iyer)
- Add additional telemetry to detect the allocation pattern earlier and trigger an automated fallback. (owner: rachel.kim)
- Ship a protective circuit-breaker that will reject the risky path for any customer with sustained error increase >1.5% for 5 min windows. (owner: ben.carter)

Customer-facing commitments:
- We will deliver a concise postmortem and remediation plan to Atlas Data by EOD 2026-08-23.
- If Atlas requests credits we’ll scope that with Finance and the account team — Mina will own the coordination.

Internal action items: please update INC-4123 with your progress and paste the verification results.

— Ben
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <pri.shah@atlasdata.com>, Jeff Nguyen <jeff.nguyen@atlasdata.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Apexx11b incident closure and follow-up (postmortem attached)

Hi Priya / Jeff —

Thanks for the quick confirmation and the additional logs you sent overnight; that helped validate the downstream webhook failure you described. Below is the high-level postmortem and next steps. Full slides attached (apexx_rca_slides_v1.pdf).

Executive summary:
- What happened: A new kernel-selection heuristic chosen for long-context inference created a memory allocation pattern that led to intermittent internal retries and 5xx/timeouts for Apexx11b in a small percentage of requests. Impact window was 07:42–08:10 PDT on 2026-08-22; Atlas Data experienced ~3.2% elevated 5xx and reported a downstream webhook failure.
- Root cause: Regression in the attention kernel selection path under a long-context memory allocation scenario.
- Remediation completed: We rolled back the kernel selector during the event and validated error rates returned to baseline within 8 minutes.

Completed follow-up actions:
1) Canary tests: Karthik ran controlled canary tests and reproduced the allocation pattern; we’ve added a reject-list rule for the heuristic pending further validation.
2) Telemetry: Rachel added an allocation-pattern metric and alerting rule to detect the condition at 0.5% deviation.
3) Circuit-breaker: Ben implemented a short-term circuit-breaker that auto-falls back for customers showing >1.0% error delta for 5 min windows; full rollout scheduled after QA.

Customer impact & credits:
- Atlas Data: Per our account conversation, we’ll propose a make-good credit scoped to the observed error window. Mina will follow up with the proposed credit amount and paperwork by 2026-08-25.

Attachments (included):
- apexx_error_wave_log_excerpt.txt — short excerpt of internal error logs with timestamps and rollback marker.
- apexx_rca_slides_v1.pdf — 2-slide executive RCA and remediation plan.

If you’d like a short sync (15–20 minutes) to walk through the slides and confirm the credit approach, we can schedule before the end of the week.

Apologies again for the disruption — we’ll keep improving our pre-deploy checks to avoid similar regressions.

Best regards,
Mina Haddad
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0142
